item.title: Paris Motor Show highlights deepening China-Europe auto cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
In the view of Serge Gachot, director of the Paris Motor Show, Chinese and European automakers have broad prospects for cooperation. He encouraged Chinese companies to invest in local production, research and development and supply chains. PARIS, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The ongoing 2026 Paris Motor Show not only features cutting-edge innovations in the auto industry, but also highlights growing opportunities for Chinese and European automakers to deepen cooperation. The week-long event, which opened on Oct. 12, brings together around 100 exhibitors and more than 60 automotive brands. A total of 25 Chinese brands, represented by 16 automakers including BYD, XPeng, Changan, Dongfeng and Leapmotor, are taking part in the show, setting a new record for Chinese participation. Serge Gachot, director of the Paris Motor Show, said that more Chinese automakers are placing greater emphasis on raising brand awareness while stepping up efforts to seek local partners, demonstrating a stronger commitment to the French and broader European markets. At the Stellantis exhibition area, Chinese automaker Leapmotor showcased its vehicles alongside European brands including Citroen and Peugeot. Leapmotor unveiled its new A05 electric compact car and flagship D19 SUV, while announcing that its B10 electric SUV had entered production at the Zaragoza plant in Spain. Developed in partnership with Stellantis and leveraging the European group's existing manufacturing infrastructure, the plant produces vehicles for the European market, marking an expansion of bilateral cooperation from sales to local manufacturing. Francesco Giacalone, head of product and marketing for Leapmotor International, said the Chinese automaker's brands complemented those of Stellantis, helping the European group reach a broader customer base and expand its market presence. Geely Automobile Holdings Limited made its first joint appearance at the show with its three brands: Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr. Nan Shengliang, vice president of Geely Auto Group and general manager of Geely Auto International Corporation, said the brand had entered 27 European countries and established more than 450 dealerships. In July, Geely Automobile Holdings and Ford Motor Company announced an agreement to produce new energy vehicles for the European market at Ford's manufacturing plant in Valencia, Spain. The arrangement is expected to help Geely accelerate its localization efforts while improving capacity utilization and supporting local employment. Marc Debord, head of communications at Volvo Car France, said that since Geely acquired Volvo Cars from Ford in 2010, sustained investment had helped Volvo accelerate the development of new platforms and powertrains, its transition to electrification and the expansion of its global business. The growing presence of Chinese automakers in Europe is also creating new opportunities for local auto parts suppliers. Francois Marion, chief communications and sustainability officer at French automotive supplier Valeo, said the company's European factories could supply components to Chinese automakers' vehicle production facilities in Europe as they expand their manufacturing footprint on the continent. Marion added that Valeo's research and development teams in China could work directly with Chinese automakers, further strengthening links between the Chinese and European automotive supply chains. Advanced driving technologies also took center stage at the show, with demonstrations extending beyond exhibition halls to the streets of Paris. XPeng and Tesla offer public test drives during the event. XPeng's Navigation Guided Pilot system has attracted interest and drawn many sign-ups for public rides. "The future of the automotive industry lies in software and artificial intelligence," said Thomas Rodier, head of marketing and communications at XPeng France. Chinese automakers' technological capabilities in these fields could also help European manufacturers accelerate their transformation, he added. In Gachot's view, Chinese and European automakers have broad prospects for cooperation. He encouraged Chinese companies to invest in local production, research and development and supply chains. Such investments would bring Chinese automakers more directly into Europe's automotive ecosystem, strengthening competition while creating further opportunities for cooperation, he said.■

item.title: Long March legacy takes root in greener landscapes of revolutionary heartlands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Perched on a hillside in Changting County of southern China, visitors soak in lush scenery stretching beside the glistening Tingjiang River. But things weren't always so picturesque. Changting, an old revolutionary base area in Fujian Province, was among the counties hardest hit by soil erosion in China's red-soil region, which threatened local people's livelihoods and left the landscape degraded. Efforts to improve the local environment began nearly a century ago. In November 1931, the Communist Party of China (CPC) established the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic in Ruijin, Jiangxi Province, where the CPC put its revolutionary ideals into governance experimentation. The following year, it launched a tree-planting campaign to protect farmland from floods and droughts, reclaim barren hills and benefit local people. During this campaign, CPC-led Red Army soldiers in Changting, which neighbors Ruijin, taught residents how to plant trees. In turn, residents brought food and seedlings to the soldiers and joined the planting campaign voluntarily. "Even amid the turmoil of war, the Party still called for tree planting with great vigor," said Chen Liping, a researcher of CPC history and local chronicles in the county. "It reflects the Party's commitment to putting people's interests first and laying the foundations for future development." As the war intensified, however, the tree-planting campaign had to be halted. The Red Army then embarked on the Long March, an epic military trek from 1934 to 1936 that broke through the encirclement of Kuomintang (Nationalist Party) forces. With some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers, the arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. As one of the starting points of the Long March, Changting has carried forward the Red Army's legacy in its decades-long efforts to combat soil erosion. Tree planting, as the Red Army had practiced earlier, remained an effective method to tackle the problem. However, in severely eroded areas, ground temperatures can soar above 70 degrees Celsius, making it difficult for trees to survive. Through experimentation, the county developed a phased approach suited to its natural conditions: first planting grass, then shrubs, and next trees, bringing the barren hills back to life step by step. "Grass helps lower ground temperatures and create favorable conditions for other vegetation, allowing a mix of tree species to take root," said Shangguan Yuanbin, deputy head of the county's soil and water conservation station. Over the years, local people adapted to changing conditions and met emerging problems with determination, patience and ingenuity. Years of effort have paid off. To date, Changting has reduced the area affected by soil erosion by about 1.17 million mu (about 78,000 hectares), while its soil erosion rate fell from 31.47 percent to 6.31 percent, according to local authorities. "Had we given up at any point over these decades, we would not have achieved such results today," said Shangguan. "We've applied the fearless Long March spirit to soil and water conservation." Changting's transformation epitomizes a broader greening trend in China, which marks a national tree-planting day annually. Official data showed that between 2021 and 2025, China accounted for roughly one-quarter of the world's increase in green vegetation, while its forest and grass coverage rate exceeded 56 percent in 2025. China's greening endeavor has gained international recognition. In 2021, Changting's comprehensive soil erosion control and ecological restoration practices were selected as a model case at the 15th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP15). But restoring the land is not the end of the story. The next challenge is to turn environmental recovery into lasting economic opportunities for local communities. One of these places is Xikuangshan, an old mining area in central China's Hunan Province. During the Long March, about 1,500 well-disciplined Red Army soldiers were stationed there for a week. Through their words and deeds, they gained the trust of locals, who went from hiding from the Red Army to following it. Dubbed the "World's Capital of Antimony," Xikuangshan has witnessed decades of intensive underground mining dating back to 1897, which led to vegetation loss, air and water pollution, and ground subsidence. Some even joked that "a white bird flying across Xikuangshan could turn black." In 2004, local people mounted an all-out campaign for ecological restoration. Inspired by the perseverance shown by the Red Army, a research team conducted countless experiments and finally achieved a breakthrough in the treatment of harmful residue generated during antimony refining, a challenge that has long confronted the industry worldwide. The once-scarred mining landscape gradually regained its vitality. The improved environment, together with its revolutionary history and mining culture, helped Xikuangshan to develop into a well-known tourist destination with around 300 million yuan (about 44.6 million U.S. dollars) in tourism revenue annually. Yang Lijun is among those who have benefited. After more than a decade, he decided to return home in 2021 upon seeing his hometown's blue skies and clear waters. He rented an abandoned rural house and opened a tourist restaurant featuring local specialties, which now generates an annual income of more than 100,000 yuan. "In the past, many residents, myself included, left home because of worsening environmental conditions," he recalled. "Now, with the environment improving, more tourists are coming, bringing new opportunities for a better life." For places like Changting and Xikuangshan, ecological restoration is therefore not simply about bringing back greenery, but also about higher-quality lives and new development paths for former revolutionary base areas. Earlier this year, China issued guidelines on accelerating the development of such areas, with measures to support systematic environmental protection and encourage eco-tourism. For Yue Hui, director of the soil and water conservation center in Changting, the changes are encouraging, but the work is far from over. "Combating soil erosion requires sustained effort. We will continue our march toward a greener future," Yue said. ■

item.title: Maduro, wife plead not guilty to new U.S. charges
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
NEW YORK, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores on Thursday pleaded not guilty to new U.S. charges of torture. The couple was brought to a Manhattan federal court to face a rewritten indictment, which accuses them of overseeing a violent system that committed torture against victims, including U.S. citizens held in Venezuelan detention. Maduro, in court, condemned the latest charges as "false accusations and false testimony," while Flores told the judge she was "completely innocent" and "not guilty." The couple was previously charged with drug trafficking and firearms crimes, to which they pleaded not guilty. The judge postponed the start of the trial by two weeks to June 14, 2027, due to the new charges. Maduro's lawyers have sought to have the case dismissed, arguing that he was the incumbent president of Venezuela at the time of his capture and was therefore entitled to immunity from foreign criminal jurisdiction. On Jan. 3, U.S. forces launched a military operation in Venezuela and forcibly seized Maduro and his wife before transporting them to New York. The couple has been held at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn since their capture in Caracas. ■

item.title: Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen named among FAO's 100 women heroes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. ROME, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese sand-control pioneer Yin Yuzhen has been named among the FAO's 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, a global recognition initiative launched by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). The honorees were celebrated at a ceremony on Thursday at the FAO headquarters in Rome as part of this year's World Food Forum. Yin has spent more than four decades combating desertification in the Maowusu Sandy Land in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. After decades of persistent tree planting, she and her family have transformed stretches of the once-barren landscape into a green expanse, overcoming harsh conditions and shifting sands. Her story also forged an enduring friendship with retired U.S. teacher Ronald Sakolsky, who raised 5,000 U.S. dollars decades ago to support her afforestation work. Yin told Xinhua that the recognition had strengthened her resolve to continue her work. "Like a Mongolian horse, I will keep pressing forward with perseverance and determination, doing my work well and giving back to nature," she said. Sitting in the audience, Sakolsky's eyes grew moist as he applauded Yin's achievement. "Yin deserves everything that she gets. She is the heroine," he told Xinhua. Addressing the ceremony, FAO Director-General Qu Dongyu hailed women farmers' roles. He said women are a driving force in agrifood systems, playing an indispensable role in food security, natural resource management, rural development and community resilience. Qu then invited Sakolsky to join Yin on stage. The two friends embraced once again and held up a trophy together. Qu said that although Sakolsky was not among the women heroes, his "passion" and "solidarity" should be recognized. Sakolsky expressed his gratitude, saying he was deeply moved by Yin's remarkable achievement. He called on everyone to plant a tree and work together to make a difference to the environment. Launched by the FAO to mark the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026, the global initiative recognizes 100 women for their outstanding contributions to agriculture, food systems and rural development. The FAO said it received 609 nominations from 131 members. The selection process involved an eligibility review, an assessment, and ranking by senior management, and two rounds of deliberations. Besides Yin, Yu Jinxiu and Dong Minfang were also among the FAO 100 Women Heroes. Yu is a moxibustion therapist from Qichun County in central China's Hubei Province, and Dong is president of the Fengrui Agricultural Machinery Professional Cooperative in Yueyang County, central China's Hunan Province. They have spent years sharing their expertise to help thousands of people secure jobs and start businesses, raising incomes for rural residents. The United Nations designated 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer to highlight women's contribution to agrifood systems and promote policies and investments that improve their access to finance, knowledge and services.

item.title: Beijing forum discusses counter-terrorism challenges posed by intelligent technologies
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
Participants communicate with each other during the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026. The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded here on Thursday. (Photo by Yue Chang/Xinhua) BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism concluded in Beijing on Thursday, with more than 320 experts and frontline personnel from 62 countries and international organizations discussing counter-terrorism challenges, including those arising from advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies. During the three-day forum, participants discussed the terrorism situation, explored solutions to common challenges, exchanged practical experience and explored avenues for international cooperation. Participants noted that the rapid development of unmanned and intelligent technologies has made terrorist activities increasingly covert and destructive, as new methods are adopted to carry out acts of terrorism and violence. They said traditional approaches that rely on individual countries acting alone and isolated prevention and control measures are increasingly inadequate to address emerging terrorist threats that are transnational, covert and enabled by intelligent technologies. The participants said combating terrorism requires countries to keep pace with advances in unmanned and intelligent technologies, strengthen their counter-terrorism capabilities, and work together to establish and improve international cooperation mechanisms for preventing and combating terrorism. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the Great Wall forum. Since its launch in 2016, the Chinese People's Armed Police Force has hosted six editions of the forum. This year's event focused on changing circumstances, evolving adversaries and technological advances, and examined the impact of artificial intelligence on efforts to prevent and combat terrorism. Discussions were organized into high-level, professional and thematic forums, creating a comprehensive, multilevel dialogue platform spanning the strategic, operational and tactical levels. An important participant in and contributor to the global fight against terrorism, China has engaged in pragmatic cooperation with other countries in terms of intelligence exchanges, border control, case investigations and counter-terrorism financing. It has also organized training sessions and seminars to share its experience with the international community and help strengthen counter-terrorism capabilities. ■ A participant interacts with a robot during the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 14, 2026. item.title: 70 years on, China's Canton Fair highlights innovation, intelligence in global trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
GUANGZHOU, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The 140th edition of the China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, opened to visitors in Guangzhou, capital of south China's Guangdong Province on Thursday, with more than 30,000 exhibiting companies and about 340,000 overseas buyers expected to attend. Serving as a barometer and wind vane of China's foreign trade, this year's fair, marking its 70th anniversary, features innovation, intelligence, greater specialization and higher quality. The Canton Fair is one of the world's few one-stop trade platforms offering a complete range of products with convenience and efficiency, while bringing together the latest products and technologies. About 64 percent of exhibitors apply new technologies such as the industrial internet and artificial intelligence (AI). New and green products account for 23.2 percent and 26 percent of the exhibits, respectively, with both hitting record highs, and more than 700 new-product launch events will be held. The fair has further enhanced its digital and intelligent operations, introducing 22 smart application scenarios and 16 AI applications for the first time, while booth navigation now covers the entire venue. "We have always worked together with exhibitors and buyers to jointly uphold the multilateral trading system and promote the building of an open world economy," said Zhu Yong, director of the China Foreign Trade Center. The 140th Canton Fair runs in three phases in Guangzhou from Oct. 15 to Nov. 4. Over the past 70 years, the Canton Fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume. ■

item.title: World Insights: Xi's principles on settling Africa's hotspot issues resonate across continent
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
NAIROBI, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The four principles proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping for resolving Africa's hotspot issues have resonated across the continent, with diplomats, scholars and media professionals hailing them as timely and practical guidance for promoting peace and development in Africa. The four principles -- adhering to the principle of "Africa-led," upholding fairness and justice, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace, and addressing both symptoms and root causes -- were put forward on Tuesday in Beijing during Xi's meeting with Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe, president of the Council of Ministers of Togo, who is on an official visit to China. Noting that the proposal comes at a time when conflicts across the continent are compounded by external interference and intensifying geopolitical rivalries, African experts said they support its emphasis on building lasting security through African ownership, international fairness, peaceful dialogue and sustainable development. AFRICAN OWNERSHIP At the heart of the four principles is the "Africa-led" approach, under which the African people are the true masters of Africa, and should play a central role in regional affairs. Claudio Rabenja, a Malagasy economist and international affairs expert, said the principle is "relevant and particularly important in the current geopolitical context," as crises in Africa stem from complex local factors that outside actors often fail to understand. "Solutions imported from or imposed by external actors do not always provide lasting answers," he said, adding that Xi's approach responds to Africa's aspiration to stop being a battleground for major-power rivalry and is consistent with China's tradition of non-interference. Similarly, Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist, said Xi's proposal "consolidates the fundamental principle of African solutions to African problems," affirming that African countries are entitled to choose their own partners and development paths while rejecting externally imposed governance agendas. Emmanuel Yenshu Vubo, dean of the Faculty of Social and Management Sciences at the University of Buea in Cameroon, said Africa "is not and cannot be reduced to mere spheres of influence or former colonial units that have only nominal independence ... Africa should be its own master." FAIRNESS AND JUSTICE The principle of upholding fairness and justice calls on all parties to abide by the principles of the UN Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned. Rabenja said respect for sovereignty and the UN Charter helps safeguard territorial integrity, curb destabilizing interventions and promote the peaceful settlement of disputes. "It is essential that African countries be able to resolve their disputes without being subjected to pressure that runs counter to their national interests," he said, noting that China's consistent stance gives African governments greater freedom to make their own choices. Gerard Njoya, editor-in-chief of Actu Chine Cameroon, said the principle reinforces the African Union (AU)'s Agenda 2063 by opposing unilateral sanctions and arbitrary interventions, addressing the long-standing demand for "an end to interference and double standards." Balew Demissie, a senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia, said the principle's call for consistent application of international law underscores the need to treat African countries fairly and with dignity. PEACE THROUGH DIALOGUE Noting that wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts, experts said the principle of promoting peace through a cessation of hostilities calls for mutual respect, extensive consultations, seeking common ground while setting aside differences, and fostering mutual understanding and accommodation. Moutlakgola Masire, a journalist at Radio Botswana, said multi-stakeholder consultations and ceasefire commitments can prevent further civilian suffering and open the way for sustainable settlements. Rabenja said military confrontation without a credible political process often fails to eliminate the root causes of violence. "Mutual concessions do not mean abandoning fundamental principles," he said. "They recognize that lasting peace often requires arrangements acceptable to all parties." China's diplomatic experience and relations with African countries can help support mediation, complementing the efforts of the AU, subregional organizations and the United Nations, he said. Njoya said ending hostilities through dialogue aligns with the AU's Silencing the Guns initiative, offering an approach to conflict resolution rooted in African values. SECURITY AND DEVELOPMENT As the principle of addressing both symptoms and root causes calls for tackling immediate security threats while pursuing long-term development, experts said China can help Africa address its challenges, citing its contributions to infrastructure construction, scholarships and vocational training across the continent. Rabenja called security and development "two inseparable dimensions of stability." Beyond protecting civilians in the short term, he said, the underlying causes of conflict -- poverty, youth unemployment, inequality and weak institutions -- must be addressed through investment in education, agriculture, energy, infrastructure and industrialization. "Security creates the conditions necessary for investment, while development reduces some of the vulnerabilities that can fuel conflict," he said. Njoya said addressing root causes is essential to achieving the goals of Agenda 2063, adding that the principle "endorses the AU's integrated approach, which seeks to tackle poverty, youth unemployment and inequality -- the underlying causes of instability." Bankuwiha said China-Africa cooperation in agriculture, industrialization, poverty alleviation, green transition and infrastructure provides the economic empowerment needed to address the structural drivers of conflict in regions such as the Horn of Africa and the Lake Chad Basin. Observers said the four principles forge "a new framework of equal partnership" that respects Africa's independent choices. "Taken together, these four principles can serve as a practical reference guide for settling past, present and future hotspot issues in Africa," Demissie said.■

item.title: China urges Japan to face history as war criminal enshrinement arrangement documents exposed
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- The documents proved once again that the Japanese government at the time knew full well the disgrace of enshrining Class-A war criminals and, fearful of the consequences, deliberately kept the decision-making process secret, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on Japanese media's disclosure for the first time of internal meeting minutes of the Yasukuni Shrine, which revealed the decision-making process of the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals including Hideki Tojo. The documents show that the Japanese government made arrangements on the enshrinement of Class-A war criminals with the shrine in as early as the 1960s, but chose to keep the public in the dark until it was revealed in 1979. These Class-A war criminals were the chief culprits behind Japanese militarists' war of aggression with the blood of innumerable war victims on their hands, Mao said, adding that the solemn verdict of the Tokyo Trials condemned them to perpetual infamy, thereby upholding international justice and laying the legal foundation for the postwar international order. "Yet those running the Japanese government have again and again paid respects to what is in fact a shrine to war criminals. One has to ask: where has the conscience gone?" she said. "History shall not be rewritten. Truth shall not be erased. Japan committed undeniable crimes during its militarist aggression. Those running the Japanese government must face history squarely, reflect on the war crimes, and make a genuine break with its militarist past," she said. ■

item.title: China's FDI equity stock ranks second globally: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- China's foreign direct investment (FDI) equity stock reached 26.8 trillion yuan (about 3.98 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, ranking second globally and marking six consecutive years of growth, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday, citing the latest annual reports from foreign-invested enterprises. A total of 461,000 foreign-invested enterprises filed annual reports last year, up 5.7 percent from 2024, according to data compiled by the ministry and other government departments. China's vast market offers foreign businesses opportunities to generate tangible returns, ministry spokesperson He Yadong told a press conference, adding that China welcomes foreign companies seeking to expand their presence in the country and share in its development opportunities. The reporting companies posted an average profit margin of 8.7 percent in 2025. In the manufacturing sector, their profit margin was 2.2 percentage points higher than that of China's major industrial enterprises, the data showed. Foreign-invested enterprises accounted for one-third of China's total goods trade and one-seventh of the country's tax revenue in 2025. They also provided an average of more than 30 million jobs annually over the past five years, the ministry said. High-tech industries have become a bright spot for foreign investment in China. FDI in the sector rose 35.1 percent year on year to 200.26 billion yuan in the first eight months of this year, official data showed. China has stepped up efforts to stabilize foreign investment and direct more capital into advanced and high-value-added sectors. A 15-measure action plan unveiled in June this year aims to expand market access, streamline investment procedures, strengthen investment promotion and improve services for foreign investors. A new version of the Catalog of Encouraged Industries for Foreign Investment also took effect on Feb. 1, encouraging foreign investment in advanced manufacturing, modern services, high-tech industries, energy conservation and environmental protection, as well as in China's central, western and northeastern regions. ■

item.title: Xi's article on advancing Party self-governance to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, will be published on Friday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 20th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It calls for upholding and strengthening overall Party leadership and persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance to turn the blueprint drawn up at the fourth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee into reality. It stresses that the Party Central Committee's major policy decisions and arrangements must be implemented with stronger determination and vigor. It also demands strengthening concrete, targeted and regular oversight of the implementation of strategic initiatives, such as applying the new development philosophy, promoting high-quality development, and accelerating the building of a new development paradigm. The article requires more scientific and effective efforts to confine power to an institutional cage. It highlights that everyone is equal before laws and regulations, with no exemptions or special privileges when observing and enforcing these rules. The article says that the fight against corruption must be pursued with greater sobriety and resolve. It describes the anti-corruption campaign as a high-stakes struggle that cannot be lost, requiring an unswerving high-pressure posture to be maintained. It further demands the timely detection, accurate identification and effective resolution of all forms of corruption, with refined anti-corruption mechanisms that align oversight actions across all sectors. ■
